title: Three Weeks and One Short Card
subtitle: 日常生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）
meta: 主题语境：日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）　|　核心词汇：menu　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 menu 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1983 the waiter ① read the menu that no customer in the teahouse would have recorded, and he said the reading was the whole of the week. The ② menu, meaning the list itself and not the card, ran three weeks and stayed unrecorded in the book; a menu, he said, is the only thing in a teahouse that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ menu in that teahouse had the same short card beside it, and the ④ menu at the far table, meaning the dish they kept for the children to pick and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A menu, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; the waiter said the recording is the part that fills three weeks.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the menu was the whole of the matter, meaning the choice and not the list. The ⑥ menu, meaning the choice and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; menu, he said, is either something you read or the only word that means both a list and a choice. He said the choice is the part they remember.

By 1988 the ⑦ menu had become a line in a bill, and the bill had become an argument about the short card. The ⑧ menu of the whole thing, the waiter wrote in March, was one teahouse and three weeks of recording; menu, he said, is either the dish at the far table or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ menu I remember is the list recorded in the bill, which closed in 1990 and is still recorded as the quietest in the teahouse. A ⑩ menu, my mother said in 1992, is the only list that improves by being recorded; every menu, she said, is a choice that has agreed to look like a list. She said the choice was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 菜单；菜谱（指茶楼里每一份旁边的那一份）
B. n. 菜单；菜谱（指那份菜单本身，与菜单卡相对）
C. 固定搭配：read the menu 看这份菜单
D. n. 菜单；菜谱（指留给孩子们点的那一道那一份）
E. n. 点菜之事（抽象总称，指一处茶楼的菜单之事）
F. n. 菜单；菜谱（指账单里写到、被记下的的那一份）
G. n. 选择、花样（指一件事里人人都点却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 花样（抽象总称，指人人都点却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: read the menu that no customer in the teahouse would have recorded
The menu, meaning the list itself and not the card
the menu at the far table
the menu was the whole of the matter
the menu had become a line in a bill
The menu of the whole thing
A menu, my mother said in 1992

answers.why: read the menu 意为“看这份菜单”，1983 年那位跑堂把茶楼里没有一位客人肯记下的一份菜单做了一遍。
menu 意为“菜单；菜谱”，指那份菜单本身而不是菜单卡，它经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被记下。
menu 意为“菜单；菜谱”，指茶楼里每一份旁边的那一份，每一份旁边都有同一张小小的菜单卡。
menu 意为“菜单；菜谱”，指最远那张桌角留给孩子们点的那一道那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
menu 意为“选择、花样”，指一件事里人人都点却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这个选择就是那件事的全部。
menu 意为“花样”，指人人都点却无人提起的那样东西而不是那份菜单，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
menu 意为“菜单；菜谱”，指账单里写到、被记下的的那一份，到 1988 年这一份成了账单里的一行。
menu 意为“点菜之事”，跑堂三月写道，整件事的菜单之事是一处茶楼和三个星期的记下。
menu 意为“菜单；菜谱”，我记得的是账单里记下过的那一份，1990 年换完了，至今仍被说成茶楼里最安静的一份。
menu 为抽象总称，母亲 1992 年说，菜单是唯一会因为被好好记下而变得更好的菜单。
